findings.summary: Each dev-dispatch run builds a fresh CostDataPlane and renders only its own facts to the same fixed filename `cost-obs.prom` in the shared node_exporter textfile directory (write_exposition's default filename; dd_runner calls it with no argument after the walk). The next development's run overwrites that file, so every prior order's launch/review/promotion/settlement facts vanish from the scrape and `sum(cost_obs_launch_total)` / `sum(cost_obs_review_total)` / `sum(cost_obs_promotion_total)` can never exceed the most recent run -- the four statistical outputs are restored for one development at a time, not for the fleet, which is what spec requirement 1 ('emitted, scraped') asks for. Concurrent runs (the fleet runs several lines at once) additionally race on that one path, and Path.write_text is not atomic, so node_exporter can scrape a truncated file and drop the whole textfile. No test covers two developments accumulating in one exposition directory.

`cost_obs_execution_cost_total` has no producer in production code: `record_execution_cost` / `record_unknown_cost` are called only from the acceptance scenario and the tests (the module docstring concedes token spend 'has no lifecycle component in this repository', which a repo-wide search confirms). So in a real run rule 1, `cost_obs:management_execution:ratio`, has no source fact and the explicit `unknown` token bucket spec requirement 3 asks to preserve is never emitted -- the deployed rules file would define a management-ratio rule that is silent, while the fixture's PASS comes entirely from facts the fixture itself mints.

Explicit missing/absence accounting is wired to exactly one terminal path. `mark_absent_if_missing` is called only from `_refused`; the `failed` (retries exhausted), `bounds` (rework limit) and `fault` terminals return without it, and dd_runner still writes the exposition afterwards. A development that dies on any of those three paths therefore emits no `cost_obs_lifecycle_present` 0 for its unproduced lifecycles -- the absent source data is silently absent rather than an observable bounded zero, which is the distinction spec requirement 3 exists to create.

The review fact's identity key is `review:{order_id}:{phase}`, so a second review of the same phase after rework is a no-op and the first verdict's label is frozen. A continuous review that REJECTs, then approves the reworked output, leaves `cost_obs_review_total{phase="continuous",verdict="reject"}` as the only series for that phase -- correct for the count the rule takes, misleading for anything reading the verdict label.
